newsitem.title: UK: BAA says Naples stake talks continuing.
newsitem.headline: BAA says Naples stake talks continuing.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc said on Wednesday it remained in discussions with the operators of Italy's Naples airport with a view to purchasing a controlling equity interest, but would not confirm a newspaper report it was about to seal a 65 percent stake.
"BAA confirms that negotiations to purchase a controlling equity stake in the operators of Naples Airport are well-advanced," the company said in a statement.
It signed a non-binding letter of intent in January last year with the airport's operator GESAC.
"If the signing of a conditional contract now goes ahead, completion will be subject to obtaining the relevant local approvals -- a process which could take up to 70 days," BAA added.
A spokeswoman said the company could not confirm a Financial Times report that it would be taking a 65 percent stake.
GESAC is currently 95 percent owned by regional and city public authorities in Naples and five percent by the national airline Alitalia.
Naples currently handles 2.5 million passengers a year, but BAA has said it sees traffic growing to 6.5 million passengers a year by 2015.
